items.title: Smooth and Sobolev configuration and reduced gauge spaces
items.statement: Fix compact connected oriented boundaryless smooth Riemannian M, d=3 or4, N>=2, smooth principal SU(N) bundle P and smooth reference A0. Define A_k=A0+H^k(T*M tensor adP), integer k>d/2+1, G_{k+1}=H^{k+1} sections of AdP, Gbar=G/Z_N, based G_m={u:u(p_m)=e}, A_infty=A0+Omega^1(adP) with seminorm C-infty topology, and smooth gauge group with C-infty section topology. Quotients have quotient topology. Define irreducible as holonomy acts irreducibly on C^N; do not replace this by full holonomy without proof. Fix action A^u=u^-1Au+u^-1du and Sobolev norms by a finite bundle atlas.
items.strategy: Specify all spaces, norm equivalence, basepoint frame and finite central quotient; locally define any unprovided adjoint-bundle/Sobolev-section conventions. Definition only; smoothness claims in the next lemma.

items.title: Sobolev gauge calculus and smooth gauge action
items.statement: For data of the preceding definition, finite-atlas Sobolev norms are equivalent; H^k sections embed in C1 for k>d/2+1, pointwise multiplication H^k x H^k→H^k is bounded, local matrix exponential/log charts make G_{k+1} a Hilbert Lie group, and the gauge action A_k x G_{k+1}→A_k is smooth.
items.strategy: Transfer existing Euclidean-domain product/embedding estimates with cutoffs; construct section charts explicitly. Prove Nemytskii derivatives and one-derivative loss, not just scalar product boundedness. Constants are uniform over the fixed finite atlas.

items.title: Gauge stabilizers and properness of the Sobolev action
items.statement: For the compact connected base and regularity above, evaluation identifies the stabilizer at A with the centralizer of Hol_A in SU(N); irreducible A has stabilizer Z_N. If A_j→A and A_j^{u_j}→B in H^k, then a subsequence u_j converges in H^{k+1}. Consequently the action of Gbar_{k+1} on A_k^* is free and proper.
items.strategy: Use parallel-transport ODE and compactness at one fibre for a uniform-convergent subsequence, then bootstrap d u=u B-A u in Sobolev norms. Supply finite-atlas proof for arbitrary smooth P/SU(N), not merely cite NR S3/SU2. Apply the inspected complex-unitary Schur statement to the holonomy representation, whose operators are bounded in finite dimension; determinant one reduces unit scalars to Z_N.

items.title: Rough-coefficient covariant Green inverse and Coulomb splitting
items.statement: For A in A_k^*, d_A^*d_A:H^{k+1}(adP)→H^{k-1}(adP) is an isomorphism with bounded inverse G_A, and H^k(T*M tensor adP)=im d_A direct-sum ker d_A^*. The bounded projection onto im d_A is d_A G_A d_A^*. The inverse and projections depend smoothly on A near each irreducible A.
items.strategy: Smooth-coefficient imported Green theorem does NOT directly cover Sobolev A. Derive distributional bootstrapping and a priori estimate from a fixed smooth reference operator plus product bounds; prove closed range/cokernel/kernel assertions and continuity of inverses. Do not use based point condition as if d_A^*d_A were surjective on its point-vanishing subspace.

items.title: Sobolev and smooth irreducible gauge-orbit principal bundles
items.statement: A_k^* is open and A_k^*→A_k^*/Gbar_{k+1} is a locally trivial smooth principal Gbar_{k+1} bundle. At A, a sufficiently small ball in A+ker d_A^* is a slice, with no intersections between different reduced-group translates; saturation is open and the orbit quotient is Hausdorff. The corresponding C-infty irreducible projection is a locally trivial topological principal Gbar_infty bundle with the actual C-infty quotient topology.
items.strategy: At (A,e), D(a,xi)=a+d_A xi is bounded iso by splitting. Banach IFT gives only near-identity uniqueness; use properness to exclude far gauge returns to a sufficiently small slice. Prove regularity/uniqueness compatibility over k to obtain C-infty local sections and continuity in every seminorm. An inverse-limit assertion alone is insufficient.

items.title: Finite holonomy witnesses for irreducibility
items.statement: For smooth connections on principal SU(N) bundles over M=S3 orS4, irreducibility is witnessed by finitely many based piecewise-smooth loop holonomies having no common proper complex invariant subspace. Such a finite tuple remains irreducible under sufficiently small connection perturbations in C1; hence A_infty^* is open.
items.strategy: Use compactness of the finite union of complex Grassmannians to extract a finite holonomy witness and continuity of parallel transport. Do not identify irreducibility with Hol_A=SU(N) for N>2. Supply the finite-dimensional Grassmannian compactness argument locally or exact earlier supplier.

items.statement: For fixed smooth principal SU(N) P over S3 orS4, every continuous map f:K→A_infty from a finite polyhedron K with f(L)⊂A_infty^* on a subpolyhedron L is homotopic relative L to a map into A_infty^*. The homotopy can be chosen arbitrarily small in any specified C-infty neighborhood of f, after retaining an irreducible neighborhood of L.

items.title: Parametric smoothing of gauge sections
items.statement: For compact smooth M and smooth principal SU(N) P, inclusion of smooth gauge sections with C-infty topology into continuous gauge sections with compact-open topology is a weak homotopy equivalence, also for the subgroup equal to identity at a chosen fibre. It induces the expected relative identifications for finite sphere/disk parameter pairs.
items.strategy: Existing ordinary homotopy-class smoothing does NOT prove continuity of families into C-infty section spaces. Prove finite-parameter relative approximation in the associated matrix bundle, then a tubular-neighborhood retraction or polar normalization preserving SU(N), identity near based fibre and boundaries. Check parameter-domain topology and collars.

items.title: Evaluation and finite-center fibrations of sphere gauge groups
items.statement: For any smooth principal SU(N) P over S^r, r=3 or4, evaluate at chosen p_m. Then G_m→G→SU(N) is a locally trivial fibre bundle, and G→Gbar=G/Z_N is a finite covering. These are fibrations to which the imported homotopy LES applies.
items.strategy: Construct local evaluation sections by a bump-supported exponential in a bundle chart, giving surjectivity by products; explicit covering neighborhoods for central action. Prove fibration hypotheses before LES; connectedness of SU(N) alone is insufficient for low homotopy iso. The low SU(N) fact is supplied by the next numerical supplier; avoid item cycles by using only fibration claims here, low-degree consequences downstream.

items.title: Low special-unitary homotopy needed for the global obstruction
items.statement: For N>=2, pi_1 SU(N)=pi_2 SU(N)=0 and pi_3 SU(N)=Z. For SU2≅S3, pi_4(S3) is finite and pi_5(S3) is nonzero.
items.strategy: Construct SU(N-1)→SU(N)→S^{2N-1} as a locally trivial bundle and prove pi1/pi2 vanishing and pi3=Z by the imported fibration LES and sphere connectivity/degree. Prove the genuinely necessary unstable inputs: pi4(S3) finite and pi5(S3) nonzero. The standard stronger computations pi4(S3)=pi5(S3)=Z2 suffice if their actual proofs are reconstructed, but no stronger numerical computation is required. Obtain/read an authoritative complete Hopf/Freudenthal/EHP/Whitehead argument or reconstruct it; Singer states the values but does not prove them, and current imported exact supplier is absent. Do not infer stable stem2 from Freudenthal without computing it. No pi4SU(N) vanishing or pi6S3 calculation is required by the final route.

items.title: Nontrivial homotopy of reduced sphere gauge groups
items.statement: For r=3 or4, N>=2 and every smooth SU(N) P→S^r, Gbar(P) has at least one nontrivial homotopy group or more than one path component.
items.strategy: For S3, pi0G=pi3SU(N)=Z and finite-center quotient changes components by only a finite image, leaving infinitely many. For S4 and N>=2, evaluation LES gives injection pi1G_m=pi5SU(N)→pi1G since pi2SU(N)=0; the finite covering injects pi1G→pi1Gbar. For N=2 use pi5(S3)≠0. For N=3, the SU2→SU3→S5 LES gives image[pi5SU3→pi5S5=Z]=kernel[Z→pi4SU2]; this kernel contains a nonzero integer since pi4SU2 is finite, hence pi5SU3≠0. For N>=4, SU(N-1)→SU(N)→S^{2N-1} stabilizes pi5 because pi5 and pi6 of those spheres vanish by dimension/connectivity. Never assume the map Z→pi4SU2 surjects, or that finite center preserves pi0; odd SU2 bundle sector can have connected Gbar. State all maps and basepoints.
